prompt: One client issues KEYS * against an instance with ten million keys, and every other client stops making progress. Why?
explanation: Command execution is single-threaded: the main thread runs commands one at a time, so a single O(N) command such as KEYS holds the entire event loop for the duration of the scan and every other client simply queues behind it.

options.text: Command execution is single-threaded, so one O(N) command delays every other client until it finishes
KEYS acquires a global write lock that other clients must wait for
The operating system throttles the network stack while KEYS runs
KEYS automatically suspends replication while it runs
